newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Northern rebel chief meets Afghan government team.
newsitem.headline: Northern rebel chief meets Afghan government team.

text.p: Northern Afghan militia commander General Abdul Rashid Dostum held talks with Kabul government representatives in the Uzbek capital of Tashkent on Wednesday, an official in his Jumbish-i-Milli faction said.
"Dostum is holding talks with government officials in Tashkent, where he had gone for medical treatment," General Fateh Mohammad, an Islamabad-based official, told Reuters.
He said Dostum had left for Tashkent four days ago and was meeting a delegation led by Afghan Interior Minister Yunus Qanuni.
Qanuni's delegation had followed Dostum to the Uzbek capital after reaching the northern town of Mazar-i-Sharif on Tuesday.
Mohammad said he had no information about the talks, but said Dostum had earlier made it clear that he would not support any attack on Kabul by the rebel Islamic Taleban militia.
The Taleban captured the key town of Sarobi, 70 km (44 miles) east of Kabul overnight, and thrust north up the Tagab Valley towards the government airbase at Bagram.
Dostum's forces control several northern provinces, but have largely stayed out of the confrontation between President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government and the Taleban.

Dostum is an opponent of Rabbani, but is despised by the Taleban for his communist background. Last month he agreed to reopen the strategic Salang highway linking Kabul with the north as part of a truce with government forces.
